title: Earning Basis on HomeFlood Cancellations: Flat, Pro Rata and Short Rate
content:
**Rule.** The earning basis fixes how much of the term premium booked for the term comes back when a HomeFlood Private Residential Flood Policies policy is cancelled on the named insured's signed request.

| Request on file | Earning basis |
|---|---|
| effective date on or before the term start | flat: the whole term premium booked for the term is returned |
| effective date after the term start, reason property sold, with a settlement statement as the supporting document | pro rata: the pro rata amount itself is returned |
| effective date after the term start, reason replaced coverage, with the replacing policy's declarations as the supporting document | pro rata: the pro rata amount itself is returned |
| any other case after the term start | short rate: 90 percent of the pro rata amount is returned |

**Pro rata amount.** The pro rata amount is the term premium booked for the term — the term premium item plus any endorsement premium items, less ENDORSEMENT and RERATE credits already given — multiplied by the days from the request's effective date to the term end, and divided by the days from the term start to the term end.

**The request on file.** The request on file is the policy's signed cancellation request — the latest received when more than one is signed, and the one recorded first among requests received on the same date; a withdrawn or unsigned request never counts — read for its reason, its effective date and its supporting document.

## Points of judgement

- **Missing document.** A property-sold request whose supporting document is not a settlement statement falls to short rate.
- **Effective date on the term start.** A request effective exactly on the term start is "on or before" it, so the cancellation is flat.
- **Reasons not listed.** Requests for no longer required or insured request, after the term start, are short rate.
